verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim lets you validate ROS 2 robot stacks through its ROS bridge, and it supports software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing of the end-to-end system. Isaac ROS packages deploy on workstations and on Jetson embedded hardware, which implies that a ROS 2-based stack can run against both sim and the real robot. However, no source explicitly states that the same code runs unchanged in both, and portability depends on structuring the stack around ROS 2. Missing for 10: an explicit documented sim-to-real 'no rewrite' workflow, details on how sim and real hardware interfaces are swapped, and independent or hands-on corroboration of code portability.
